1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

482: +		t.Fatal("expected a missing netdev to be detected")
483: +	}
484: +	if ovsDeviceMissing("[]") {
485: +		t.Fatal("a live interface reports an empty error set")
486: +	}
487: +	if !clabAutoPort.MatchString("clab-1f57ad50") {
488: +		t.Fatal("expected a containerlab auto port name to match")
489: +	}

491: +		t.Fatal("topology interface names are not auto ports")
492: +	}

494: +		t.Fatalf("ovsMapValue() = %q", got)
495: +	}

497: +		t.Fatalf("ovsMapValue() = %q", got)

507: +func TestOVSEndpointPortDoesNotAccumulate(t *testing.T) {
508: +	if os.Geteuid() != 0 {
509: +		t.Skip("requires root")
510: +	}
511: +	if _, err := exec.LookPath("ovs-vsctl"); err != nil {
512: +		t.Skip("ovs-vsctl not found")
513: +	}
514: +
515: +	// ixr-dut-30-e1-1 is 15 characters, so it is the OVS port name.
516: +	// ixr-dut-30-e1-10 is 16 and is recorded as a clab-* port instead.
517: +	for _, endpoint := range []string{"ixr-dut-30-e1-1", "ixr-dut-30-e1-10"} {
518: +		t.Run(endpoint, func(t *testing.T) {
519: +			assertReattachKeepsOnePort(t, endpoint)
520: +		})
521: +	}
522: +}
523: +
524: +func assertReattachKeepsOnePort(t *testing.T, endpoint string) {
525: +	t.Helper()
526: +
527: +	bridge := "br-ovs-leak"
528: +	c := goOvs.New()
529: +	_ = c.VSwitch.DeleteBridge(bridge)
530: +	if err := c.VSwitch.AddBridge(bridge); err != nil {
531: +		t.Skipf("ovsdb is not available: %v", err)
532: +	}
533: +	t.Cleanup(func() {
534: +		_ = goOvs.New().VSwitch.DeleteBridge(bridge)
535: +	})
536: +
537: +	n := &ovs{}
538: +	if err := n.Init(&clabtypes.NodeConfig{ShortName: bridge}); err != nil {
539: +		t.Fatalf("init: %v", err)
540: +	}
541: +	ep := clablinks.NewEndpointBridge(
542: +		clablinks.NewEndpointGeneric(n, endpoint, nil),
543: +		false,
544: +	)
545: +	if err := n.AddEndpoint(ep); err != nil {
546: +		t.Fatalf("add endpoint: %v", err)
547: +	}
548: +
549: +	first, peer := addVethPair(t)
550: +	if err := n.AddLinkToContainer(
551: +		context.Background(),
552: +		first,
553: +		clablinks.SetNameMACAndUpInterface(first, ep),
554: +	); err != nil {
555: +		t.Fatalf("add link: %v", err)
556: +	}
557: +	if err := netlink.LinkDel(peer); err != nil {
558: +		t.Fatalf("delete peer: %v", err)
559: +	}
560: +	if ports := dataPorts(t, bridge); len(ports) != 1 {
561: +		t.Fatalf("peer delete left %v, want the stale port", ports)
562: +	}
563: +
564: +	// An untagged port may belong to the operator and is not removed for a topology interface.
565: +	if out, err := ovsVsctl("--no-wait", "add-port", bridge, "operator-port"); err != nil {
566: +		t.Fatalf("add operator port: %v (%s)", err, out)
567: +	}
568: +	if err := n.DeleteBridgePort("operator-port"); err != nil {
569: +		t.Fatalf("delete bridge port: %v", err)
570: +	}
571: +	if ports := dataPorts(t, bridge); len(ports) != 2 {
572: +		t.Fatalf("ports after untagged delete = %v, want the operator port kept", ports)
573: +	}
574: +	if err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(bridge, "operator-port"); err != nil {
575: +		t.Fatalf("delete operator port: %v", err)
576: +	}
577: +
578: +	// A port named after the interface keeps its config across a reattach.
579: +	isNamedPort := dataPorts(t, bridge)[0] == endpoint
580: +	if isNamedPort {
581: +		if out, err := ovsVsctl("set", "Port", endpoint, "tag=100"); err != nil {
582: +			t.Fatalf("set tag: %v (%s)", err, out)
583: +		}
584: +	}
585: +
586: +	second, secondPeer := addVethPair(t)
587: +	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = netlink.LinkDel(secondPeer) })
588: +	if err := n.AddLinkToContainer(
589: +		context.Background(),
590: +		second,
591: +		clablinks.SetNameMACAndUpInterface(second, ep),
592: +	); err != nil {
593: +		t.Fatalf("reattach: %v", err)
594: +	}
595: +	if ports := dataPorts(t, bridge); len(ports) != 1 {
596: +		t.Fatalf("ports after reattach = %v, want 1", ports)
597: +	}
598: +	if isNamedPort {
599: +		out, err := ovsVsctl("get", "Port", endpoint, "tag")
600: +		if err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(string(out)) != "100" {
601: +			t.Fatalf("tag after reattach = %q, err = %v, want 100", out, err)
602: +		}
603: +	}
604: +
605: +	if err := n.Delete(context.Background()); err != nil {
606: +		t.Fatalf("delete node: %v", err)
607: +	}
608: +	if ports := dataPorts(t, bridge); len(ports) != 0 {
609: +		t.Fatalf("ports after node delete = %v", ports)
610: +	}
611: +}
612: +
613: +func addVethPair(t *testing.T) (netlink.Link, netlink.Link) {
614: +	t.Helper()
615: +
616: +	name := clablinks.NewEndpointGeneric(nil, "x", nil).GetRandIfaceName()
617: +	peerName := name + "p"
618: +	veth := &netlink.Veth{
619: +		LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{Name: name},
620: +		PeerName:  peerName,
621: +	}
622: +	if err := netlink.LinkAdd(veth); err != nil {
623: +		t.Fatalf("add veth: %v", err)
624: +	}
625: +	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(name)
626: +	if err != nil {
627: +		t.Fatalf("lookup veth: %v", err)
628: +	}
629: +	peer, err := netlink.LinkByName(peerName)
630: +	if err != nil {
631: +		t.Fatalf("lookup peer: %v", err)
632: +	}
633: +
634: +	return link, peer
635: +}
636: +
637: +func dataPorts(t *testing.T, bridge string) []string {
638: +	t.Helper()
639: +
640: +	ports, err := goOvs.New().VSwitch.ListPorts(bridge)
641: +	if err != nil {
642: +		t.Fatalf("list ports: %v", err)
643: +	}
644: +	var data []string
645: +	for _, port := range ports {
646: +		if port != bridge {
647: +			data = append(data, port)
648: +		}
649: +	}
650: +
651: +	return data
652: +}

19: 	// Deploy deploys this endpoint through its associated link.
20: 	Deploy(context.Context) error

34: 	Verify(context.Context, *VerifyLinkParams) error
35: 	// HasSameNodeAndInterface returns true if an endpoint that implements this interface
36: 	// has the same node and interface name as the given endpoint.
37: 	HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept Endpoint) bool
38: 	Remove(context.Context) error
39: 	// Activate brings this endpoint's interface up in its current namespace.

60: 	// Link is the link this endpoint belongs to.
61: 	Link     Link
62: 	MAC      net.HardwareAddr

65: 	IPv6     netip.Prefix
66: 	Vars     map[string]any

69: func NewEndpointGeneric(node Node, iface string, link Link) *EndpointGeneric {
70: 	return &EndpointGeneric{
71: 		Node:       node,
72: 		IfaceName:  iface,
73: 		IfaceAlias: "",
74: 		// random name is generated for the endpoint to avoid name collisions
75: 		// when it is first deployed in the root namespace
76: 		randName: genRandomIfName(),
77: 		Link:     link,
78: 		Vars:     make(map[string]any),
79: 	}
80: }

97: 	}

141: func (e *EndpointGeneric) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
142: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
143: 		brSideEp, err := netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(e.GetIfaceName()))
144: 		_, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError)
145: 
146: 		switch {
147: 		case notfound:
148: 			// The netdev may already be gone while its bridge port is not, which is how OVS
149: 			// keeps a port whose name is not the topology interface name.
150: 			return removeBridgePort(e.GetNode(), e.GetIfaceName())
151: 		case err != nil:
152: 			return err
153: 		}
154: 		log.Debugf(
155: 			"Removing interface %q from namespace %q",
156: 			e.GetIfaceName(),
157: 			e.GetNode().GetShortName(),
158: 		)
159: 		if err = netlink.LinkDel(brSideEp); err != nil {
160: 			return err
161: 		}
162: 
163: 		return removeBridgePort(e.GetNode(), e.GetIfaceName())
164: 	})
165: }

167: // moveEndpoint moves the endpoint's interface into dst's namespace and transfers ownership.
168: // The interface is left in the DOWN state; callers that need it active should follow up with
169: // Endpoint.Activate once all endpoints are in place.
170: func moveEndpoint(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint, dst Node) error {
171: 	src := e.GetNode()
172: 	if src == nil {
173: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %q has no source node", e.GetIfaceName())
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	if dst == nil {
177: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %q has no destination node", e.GetIfaceName())
178: 	}
179: 
180: 	if src == dst {
181: 		return nil
182: 	}
183: 
184: 	if !slices.Contains(src.GetEndpoints(), e) {
185: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q does not own endpoint %q", src.GetShortName(), e.GetIfaceName())
186: 	}
187: 
188: 	for _, owned := range dst.GetEndpoints() {
189: 		if owned == e {
190: 			return fmt.Errorf(
191: 				"node %q already owns endpoint %q",
192: 				dst.GetShortName(),
193: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
194: 			)
195: 		}
196: 		if owned.GetIfaceName() == e.GetIfaceName() {
197: 			return fmt.Errorf(
198: 				"node %q already tracks interface %q",
199: 				dst.GetShortName(),
200: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
201: 			)
202: 		}
203: 	}
204: 
205: 	if err := ensureOwnershipAltName(ctx, e); err != nil {
206: 		return err
207: 	}
208: 
209: 	if err := moveLink(ctx, src, e.GetIfaceName(), dst); err != nil {
210: 		return err
211: 	}
212: 
213: 	if err := src.ReleaseEndpoint(e); err != nil {
214: 		return err
215: 	}
216: 	e.SetNode(dst)
217: 	if err := dst.AdoptEndpoint(e); err != nil {
218: 		e.SetNode(src)
219: 		_ = src.AdoptEndpoint(e)
220: 		return fmt.Errorf(
221: 			"endpoint %q moved but destination ownership update failed: %w",
222: 			e.GetIfaceName(),
223: 			err,
224: 		)
225: 	}
226: 
227: 	return nil
228: }
229: 
230: // Activate brings the endpoint's interface up in its current namespace.
231: func (e *EndpointGeneric) Activate(ctx context.Context) error {
232: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
233: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
234: 		if err != nil {
235: 			return err
236: 		}
237: 		return netlink.LinkSetUp(link)
238: 	})
239: }
240: 
241: func ensureOwnershipAltName(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
242: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
243: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
244: 		if err != nil {
245: 			return err
246: 		}
247: 
248: 		return addOwnershipAltName(link, e)
249: 	})
250: }
251: 
252: // HasSameNodeAndInterface returns true if the given endpoint has the same node and interface name
253: // as the `ept` endpoint.
254: func (e *EndpointGeneric) HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept Endpoint) bool {
255: 	return e.Node == ept.GetNode() && e.IfaceName == ept.GetIfaceName()
256: }
257: 
258: func (e *EndpointGeneric) String() string {
259: 	ifDisplayName := e.IfaceName
260: 	if e.IfaceAlias != "" {
261: 		ifDisplayName += fmt.Sprintf(" (%s)", e.IfaceAlias)
262: 	}
263: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", e.Node.GetShortName(), ifDisplayName)
264: }
265: 
266: // CheckEndpointUniqueness checks that the given endpoint appears only once for the node
267: // it is assigned to.
268: func CheckEndpointUniqueness(e Endpoint) error {
269: 	for _, ept := range e.GetNode().GetEndpoints() {
270: 		if e == ept {
271: 			// since node contains all endpoints including the one we are checking
272: 			// we skip it
273: 			continue
274: 		}
275: 		// if `e` has the same node and interface name as `ept` then we have a duplicate
276: 		if e.HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept) {
277: 			return fmt.Errorf("duplicate endpoint %s", e)
278: 		}
279: 	}
280: 
281: 	return nil
282: }
283: 
284: // CheckEndpointExists checks that a certain
285: // interface exists in the network namespace of the given node.
286: func CheckEndpointExists(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
287: 	err := CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet(ctx, e)
288: 	if err == nil {
289: 		return fmt.Errorf("interface %q does not exist", e.String())
290: 	}
291: 	return nil
292: }
293: 
294: // CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet verifies that the interface referenced in the
295: // provided endpoint does not yet exist in the referenced node.
296: func CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
297: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
298: 		// we expect a netlink.LinkNotFoundError when querying for
299: 		// the interface with the given endpoints name
300: 		var err error
301: 		_, err = netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
302: 
303: 		if _, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError); notfound {
304: 			return nil
305: 		}
306: 
307: 		return fmt.Errorf(
308: 			"interface %s is defined via topology but already exists: %v",
309: 			e.String(),
310: 			err,
311: 		)
312: 	})
313: }
314: 
315: func moveLink(ctx context.Context, src Node, ifaceName string, dst Node) error {
316: 	return src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
317: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ifaceName)
318: 		if err != nil {
319: 			return err
320: 		}
321: 
322: 		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
323: 			return err
324: 		}
325: 
326: 		return dst.AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
327: 			return nil
328: 		})
329: 	})
330: }

236: 
237: 	if _, ok := node.(*mgmtBridgeLinkNode); ok && ownerName == mgmtNetOwnerName {
238: 		return HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, node.GetShortName(), ifaceName)
239: 	}
240:

7: import (

28: const (
29: 	ovsEndpointExtID = "containerlab-endpoint"
30: 	// ovsTimeoutSeconds bounds ovs-vsctl calls, which wait forever when ovs-vswitchd is down.
31: 	ovsTimeoutSeconds = 30
32: )
33: 
34: // clabAutoPort matches the random netdev name used when the topology interface name is not a
35: // valid Linux name. Those netdevs are what Open vSwitch records as the port name.
36: var clabAutoPort = regexp.MustCompile(`^clab-[0-9a-f]{8}$`)
37: 
38: var kindNames = []string{"ovs-bridge"}
39: 
40: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
41: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
42: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
43: 		return new(ovs)
44: 	}, nil)
45: }

47: type ovs struct {
48: 	clabnodes.DefaultNode
49: }
50: 
51: func (n *ovs) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
52: 	// Init DefaultNode
53: 	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
54: 
55: 	n.Cfg = cfg
56: 	for _, o := range opts {
57: 		o(n)
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	n.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased = true
61: 
62: 	return nil
63: }
64: 
65: func (n *ovs) CheckDeploymentConditions(_ context.Context) error {
66: 	// check if ovs bridge exists
67: 	c := goOvs.New()
68: 
69: 	// We were previously doing c.VSwitch.Get.Bridge() but it doesn't work
70: 	// when the bridge has a protocol version higher than 1.0
71: 	// So listing the bridges is safer
72: 	bridges, err := c.VSwitch.ListBridges()
73: 	if err != nil {
74: 		return fmt.Errorf("error while listing ovs bridges: %v", err)
75: 	}
76: 	if !clabinternalslices.Contains(bridges, n.Cfg.ShortName) {
77: 		return fmt.Errorf("could not find ovs bridge %q", n.Cfg.ShortName)
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	return nil
81: }
82: 
83: func (n *ovs) Deploy(_ context.Context, _ *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
84: 	n.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)
85: 	return nil
86: }
87: 
88: func (*ovs) PullImage(_ context.Context) error             { return nil }
89: func (*ovs) GetImages(_ context.Context) map[string]string { return map[string]string{} }
90: 
91: func (n *ovs) Delete(_ context.Context) error {
92: 	c := goOvs.New(goOvs.Timeout(ovsTimeoutSeconds))
93: 
94: 	for _, ep := range n.GetEndpoints() {
95: 		// Under the hood, this is called with "--if-exists", so it will handle the case where it
96: 		// doesn't exist for some reason.
97: 		err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, ep.GetIfaceName())
98: 		if err == nil {
99: 			err = n.removeEndpointPorts(ep.GetIfaceName())
100: 		}
101: 		if err != nil {
102: 			log.Errorf(
103: 				"Could not remove OVS port %q from bridge %q: %v",
104: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
105: 				n.Config().ShortName,
106: 				err,
107: 			)
108: 		}
109: 	}
110: 
111: 	// One sweep for ports created before they were tagged. Per-endpoint deletion already
112: 	// removes ports this version tagged at attach time.
113: 	if err := n.removeMissingAutoPorts(); err != nil {
114: 		log.Errorf(
115: 			"Could not remove stale OVS ports from bridge %q: %v",
116: 			n.Config().ShortName,
117: 			err,
118: 		)
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	return nil
122: }
123: 
124: // DeleteBridgePort removes the OVS port containerlab tagged for one topology interface. Untagged
125: // ports may belong to the operator, so only Delete removes a port by its name.
126: func (n *ovs) DeleteBridgePort(endpoint string) error {
127: 	return n.removeEndpointPorts(endpoint)
128: }

130: func (*ovs) DeleteNetnsSymlink() (err error) { return nil }

133: func (*ovs) UpdateConfigWithRuntimeInfo(_ context.Context) error { return nil }
134: 
135: // GetContainers is a noop for bridges.
136: func (*ovs) GetContainers(_ context.Context) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
137: 	return nil, nil
138: }

140: // RunExec is noop for ovs kind.
141: func (n *ovs) RunExec(_ context.Context, _ *clabexec.ExecCmd) (*clabexec.ExecResult, error) {
142: 	log.Warnf("Exec operation is not implemented for kind %q", n.Config().Kind)
143: 
144: 	return nil, clabexec.ErrRunExecNotSupported
145: }

147: func (n *ovs) AddLinkToContainer(
148: 	ctx context.Context,
149: 	link netlink.Link,
150: 	f func(ns.NetNS) error,
151: ) error {
152: 	// retrieve the namespace handle
153: 	curNamespace, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
154: 	if err != nil {
155: 		return err
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	// execute the given function
159: 	err = curNamespace.Do(f)
160: 	if err != nil {
161: 		return err
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	// need to reread the link, due to the changed the function f might have applied to
165: 	// the link. Usually it renames the link to its final name.
166: 	link, err = netlink.LinkByIndex(link.Attrs().Index)
167: 	if err != nil {
168: 		return err
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	name := link.Attrs().Name
172: 	logical := n.logicalEndpointName(link)
173: 	args := []string{"--may-exist", "add-port", n.Cfg.ShortName, name}
174: 	// A port named after the interface is reused by --may-exist and keeps its config. A random
175: 	// netdev name needs a tag, so that a later attach or link removal can find the port. The full
176: 	// stale-port sweep runs once from Delete, not on every attach.
177: 	if logical != name {
178: 		if err := n.removeEndpointPorts(logical); err != nil {
179: 			return err
180: 		}
181: 		args = append(args,
182: 			"--", "set", "Interface", name,
183: 			"external_ids:"+ovsEndpointExtID+"="+ovsMapValue(logical),
184: 		)
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	out, err := ovsVsctl(args...)
188: 	if err != nil {
189: 		return fmt.Errorf("add OVS port %q as %q: %w (%s)", name, logical, err, out)
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	return nil
193: }

195: func (m *ovs) GetLinkEndpointType() clablinks.LinkEndpointType {
196: 	return clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridge
197: }

199: // logicalEndpointName is the topology interface name for link. When that name is not a valid
200: // Linux interface name, the netdev keeps a random clab-* name and the topology name is an altname.
201: func (n *ovs) logicalEndpointName(link netlink.Link) string {
202: 	if link == nil {
203: 		return ""
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	name := link.Attrs().Name
207: 	alts := make(map[string]struct{}, len(link.Attrs().AltNames))
208: 	for _, alt := range link.Attrs().AltNames {
209: 		alts[alt] = struct{}{}
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	for _, ep := range n.GetEndpoints() {
213: 		iface := ep.GetIfaceName()
214: 		if iface == name {
215: 			return iface
216: 		}
217: 		if _, ok := alts[clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(iface)]; ok {
218: 			return iface
219: 		}
220: 	}
221: 
222: 	return name
223: }
224: 
225: // removeEndpointPorts deletes the ports on this bridge tagged with the topology interface name.
226: func (n *ovs) removeEndpointPorts(endpoint string) error {
227: 	if endpoint == "" || n.Cfg == nil || n.Cfg.ShortName == "" {
228: 		return nil
229: 	}
230: 
231: 	c := goOvs.New(goOvs.Timeout(ovsTimeoutSeconds))
232: 
233: 	names, err := ovsInterfaceNames(
234: 		"external_ids:" + ovsEndpointExtID + "=" + ovsMapValue(endpoint),
235: 	)
236: 	if err != nil {
237: 		return err
238: 	}
239: 
240: 	onBridge, err := bridgePortSet(c, n.Cfg.ShortName)
241: 	if err != nil {
242: 		return err
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	for _, name := range names {
246: 		if _, ok := onBridge[name]; !ok {
247: 			continue
248: 		}
249: 		if err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, name); err != nil {
250: 			return err
251: 		}
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	return nil
255: }
256: 
257: // removeMissingAutoPorts deletes clab-* ports whose netdev is already gone. Deleting the container
258: // side of the veth removes the device and leaves the OVS port in place under that random name.
259: func (n *ovs) removeMissingAutoPorts() error {
260: 	if n.Cfg == nil || n.Cfg.ShortName == "" {
261: 		return nil
262: 	}
263: 
264: 	c := goOvs.New(goOvs.Timeout(ovsTimeoutSeconds))
265: 	ports, err := c.VSwitch.ListPorts(n.Cfg.ShortName)
266: 	if err != nil {
267: 		return err
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	for _, port := range ports {
271: 		if !clabAutoPort.MatchString(port) {
272: 			continue
273: 		}
274: 		missing, err := ovsInterfaceDeviceMissing(port)
275: 		if err != nil {
276: 			return err
277: 		}
278: 		if !missing {
279: 			continue
280: 		}
281: 		log.Debugf(
282: 			"Removing stale OVS port %q from bridge %q",
283: 			port,
284: 			n.Cfg.ShortName,
285: 		)
286: 		if err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, port); err != nil {
287: 			return err
288: 		}
289: 	}
290: 
291: 	return nil
292: }
293: 
294: func bridgePortSet(c *goOvs.Client, bridge string) (map[string]struct{}, error) {
295: 	ports, err := c.VSwitch.ListPorts(bridge)
296: 	if err != nil {
297: 		return nil, err
298: 	}
299: 
300: 	set := make(map[string]struct{}, len(ports))
301: 	for _, port := range ports {
302: 		set[port] = struct{}{}
303: 	}
304: 
305: 	return set, nil
306: }
307: 
308: func ovsVsctl(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
309: 	args = append([]string{fmt.Sprintf("--timeout=%d", ovsTimeoutSeconds)}, args...)
310: 
311: 	return exec.Command("ovs-vsctl", args...).CombinedOutput()
312: }
313: 
314: func ovsInterfaceNames(condition string) ([]string, error) {
315: 	out, err := ovsVsctl(
316: 		"--format=csv",
317: 		"--no-headings",
318: 		"--data=bare",
319: 		"--columns=name",
320: 		"find",
321: 		"Interface",
322: 		condition,
323: 	)
324: 	if err != nil {
325: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("find OVS interfaces: %w (%s)", err, out)
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	text := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
329: 	if text == "" {
330: 		return nil, nil
331: 	}
332: 
333: 	return strings.Split(text, "\n"), nil
334: }
335: 
336: func ovsInterfaceDeviceMissing(iface string) (bool, error) {
337: 	out, err := ovsVsctl("--data=bare", "get", "Interface", iface, "error")
338: 	if err != nil {
339: 		// The port disappeared between ListPorts and this get. Nothing left to delete.
340: 		if ovsRowMissing(string(out)) {
341: 			return false, nil
342: 		}
343: 		return false, fmt.Errorf("get OVS interface %q error: %w (%s)", iface, err, out)
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	return ovsDeviceMissing(string(out)), nil
347: }
348: 
349: // ovsDeviceMissing reports whether an OVS interface error column says the netdev is gone.
350: // A live interface returns "[]".
351: func ovsDeviceMissing(errorColumn string) bool {
352: 	errorColumn = strings.TrimSpace(errorColumn)
353: 
354: 	return strings.Contains(errorColumn, "could not open network device")
355: }
356: 
357: func ovsRowMissing(output string) bool {
358: 	return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(output), "no row")
359: }
360: 
361: func ovsMapValue(value string) string {
362: 	if value == "" {
363: 		return `""`
364: 	}
365: 	for _, r := range value {
366: 		switch {
367: 		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
368: 		case strings.ContainsRune("-_.:@", r):
369: 		default:
370: 			return fmt.Sprintf("%q", value)
371: 		}
372: 	}
373: 
374: 	return value
375: }

{\n\tclabnodes.DefaultNode\n}\n\nfunc (n *ovs) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {\n\t// Init DefaultNode\n\tn.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)\n\n\tn.Cfg = cfg\n\tfor _, o := range opts {\n\t\to(n)\n\t}\n\n\tn.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased = true\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (n *ovs) CheckDeploymentConditions(_ context.Context) error {\n\t// check if ovs bridge n.Cfg.ShortName) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"could not find ovs bridge %q\", n.Cfg.ShortName)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (n *ovs) Deploy(_ context.Context, _ *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {\n\tn.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (*ovs) PullImage(_ context.Context) error             { return nil }\nfunc (*ovs) GetImages(_ context.Context) map[string]string { return map[string]string{} }\n\nfunc (n *ovs) Delete(_ context.Context) error {\n\tc := goOvs.New(goOvs.Timeout(ovsTimeoutSeconds))\n\n\tfor _, ep := range n.GetEndpoints() {\n\t\t// Under the hood, this is called with \"--if-exists\", so it will handle the case where it\n\t\t// doesn't exist for some reason.\n\t\terr := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, ep.GetIfaceName())\n\t\tif err == nil {\n\t\t\terr = n.removeEndpointPorts(ep.GetIfaceName())\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"Could not remove OVS port %q from bridge %q: %v\",\n\t\t\t\tep.GetIfaceName(),\n\t\t\t\tn.Config().ShortName,\n\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// One sweep for ports created before they were tagged. Per-endpoint deletion already\n\t// removes ports this version tagged at attach time.\n\tif err := n.removeMissingAutoPorts(); err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\"Could not remove stale OVS ports from bridge %q: %v\",\n\t\t\tn.Config().ShortName,\n\t\t\terr,\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// DeleteBridgePort removes the OVS port containerlab tagged for one topology interface. 24: var kindNames = []string{"ovs-bridge"}

26: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
27: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
28: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
29: 		return new(ovs)
30: 	}, nil)
31: }

33: type ovs struct {
34: 	clabnodes.DefaultNode
35: }
36: 
37: func (n *ovs) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
38: 	// Init DefaultNode
39: 	n.DefaultNode = *clabnodes.NewDefaultNode(n)
40: 
41: 	n.Cfg = cfg
42: 	for _, o := range opts {
43: 		o(n)
44: 	}
45: 
46: 	n.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased = true
47: 
48: 	return nil
49: }
50: 
51: func (n *ovs) CheckDeploymentConditions(_ context.Context) error {
52: 	// check if ovs bridge exists
53: 	c := goOvs.New()
54: 
55: 	// We were previously doing c.VSwitch.Get.Bridge() but it doesn't work
56: 	// when the bridge has a protocol version higher than 1.0
57: 	// So listing the bridges is safer
58: 	bridges, err := c.VSwitch.ListBridges()
59: 	if err != nil {
60: 		return fmt.Errorf("error while listing ovs bridges: %v", err)
61: 	}
62: 	if !clabinternalslices.Contains(bridges, n.Cfg.ShortName) {
63: 		return fmt.Errorf("could not find ovs bridge %q", n.Cfg.ShortName)
64: 	}
65: 
66: 	return nil
67: }
68: 
69: func (n *ovs) Deploy(_ context.Context, _ *clabnodes.DeployParams) error {
70: 	n.SetState(clabnodesstate.Deployed)
71: 	return nil
72: }

74: func (*ovs) PullImage(_ context.Context) error             { return nil }
75: func (*ovs) GetImages(_ context.Context) map[string]string { return map[string]string{} }
76: 
77: func (n *ovs) Delete(_ context.Context) error {
78: 	c := goOvs.New()
79: 
80: 	for _, ep := range n.GetEndpoints() {
81: 		// Under the hood, this is called with "--if-exists", so it will handle the case where it
82: 		// doesn't exist for some reason.
83: 		if err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, ep.GetIfaceName()); err != nil {
84: 			log.Errorf(
85: 				"Could not remove OVS port %q from bridge %q",
86: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
87: 				n.Config().ShortName,
88: 			)
89: 		}
90: 	}
91: 
92: 	return nil
93: }

Endpoint is the endpoint that triggers the creation of the link.\nfunc (b *Bridge) Deploy(ctx context.Context, endpoint Endpoint) error {\n\terr := endpoint.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(nn ns.NetNS) error {\n\t\t// add the bridge\n\t\terr := netlink.LinkAdd(&netlink.Bridge{\n\t\t\tLinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{\n\t\t\t\tName: b.endpoint.GetIfaceName(),\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t})\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\t// retrieve link ref\n\t\tnetlinkLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(b.endpoint.GetIfaceName())\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn SetNameMACAndUpInterface(netlinkLink, b.endpoint)(nn)\n\t})\n\n\treturn err\n}\n\nfunc (*Bridge) PostDeploy(context.Context) error {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// Remove removes the link.\nfunc (b *Bridge) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {\n\t// check Deployment state, if the Link was already\n\t// removed via e.g. the peer node\n\tif b.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\t// trigger link removal via the NodeEndpoint\n\terr := b.endpoint.Remove(ctx)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Debug(err)\n\t}\n\t// adjust the Deployment status to reflect the removal\n\tb.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// GetType returns the type of the link.\nfunc (b *Bridge) GetType() LinkType {\n\treturn LinkTypeBridge\n}\n\n// GetEndpoints returns the endpoints of the link.\nfunc (b *Bridge) GetEndpoints() []Endpoint {\n\treturn []Endpoint{b.endpoint}\n}\n\nfunc (b *Bridge) GetRuntimeEndpoints() []Endpoint {\n\treturn b.GetEndpoints()\n}\n\n// GetMTU returns the Link MTU.\nfunc (b *Bridge) GetMTU() int {\n\treturn b.MTU\n}",

12: // EndpointRaw is the raw (string) representation of an endpoint as defined in the topology file
13: // for a given link definition.
14: type EndpointRaw struct {
15: 	Node  string         `yaml:"node"`

18: 	IPv4  string         `yaml:"ipv4,omitempty"`

20: 	Vars  map[string]any `yaml:"vars,omitempty"`
21: }

23: // NewEndpointRaw creates a new EndpointRaw struct.
24: func NewEndpointRaw(node, nodeIf, mac string) *EndpointRaw {
25: 	return &EndpointRaw{
26: 		Node:  node,
27: 		Iface: nodeIf,
28: 		MAC:   mac,
29: 	}
30: }
31: 
32: // Resolve resolves the EndpointRaw into an Endpoint interface that is implemented
33: // by a concrete endpoint struct such as EndpointBridge, EndpointHost, EndpointVeth.
34: // The type of an endpoint is determined by the node it belongs to.
35: // Resolving a raw endpoint adds an associated Link and Node to the endpoint.
36: // It also adds the endpoint to the node.
37: func (er *EndpointRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams, l Link) (Endpoint, error) {
38: 	// check if the referenced node does exist
39: 	node, exists := params.Nodes[er.Node]
40: 	if !exists {
41: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to find node %s", er.Node)
42: 	}
43: 
44: 	genericEndpoint := NewEndpointGeneric(node, er.Iface, l)
45: 
46: 	if er.IPv4 != "" {
47: 		p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(er.IPv4)
48: 		if err != nil || !p.Addr().Is4() {
49: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
50: 				"invalid ipv4 address %q for %s:%s",
51: 				er.IPv4,
52: 				er.Node,
53: 				er.Iface,
54: 			)
55: 		}
56: 		genericEndpoint.IPv4 = p
57: 	}
58: 
59: 	if er.IPv6 != "" {
60: 		p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(er.IPv6)
61: 		if err != nil || !p.Addr().Is6() {
62: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
63: 				"invalid ipv6 address %q for %s:%s",
64: 				er.IPv6,
65: 				er.Node,
66: 				er.Iface,
67: 			)
68: 		}
69: 		genericEndpoint.IPv6 = p
70: 	}
71: 
72: 	// Normalize vars to ensure JSON serialization compatibility
73: 	// (converts map[interface{}]interface{} to map[string]any)
74: 	genericEndpoint.Vars = normalizeVars(er.Vars)
75: 
76: 	var err error
77: 	if er.MAC == "" {
78: 		// if mac is not present generate one
79: 		genericEndpoint.MAC, err = clabutils.GenMac(clabconstants.ClabOUI)
80: 		if err != nil {
81: 			return nil, err
82: 		}
83: 	} else {
84: 		// if MAC is present, set it
85: 		m, err := net.ParseMAC(er.MAC)
86: 		if err != nil {
87: 			return nil, err
88: 		}
89: 		genericEndpoint.MAC = m
90: 	}
91: 
92: 	var e Endpoint
93: 
94: 	switch node.GetLinkEndpointType() {
95: 	case LinkEndpointTypeBridge, LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS:
96: 		e = NewEndpointBridge(genericEndpoint, false)
97: 
98: 	case LinkEndpointTypeHost:
99: 		e = NewEndpointHost(genericEndpoint)
100: 
101: 	case LinkEndpointTypeVeth:
102: 		e = NewEndpointVeth(genericEndpoint)
103: 	}
104: 	if l.GetType() == LinkTypeDummy {
105: 		e = NewEndpointDummy(genericEndpoint)
106: 	}
107: 	// also add the endpoint to the node
108: 	err = node.AddEndpoint(e)
109: 	if err != nil {
110: 		return nil, err
111: 	}
112: 
113: 	return e, nil
114: }

Reasoning
So for a link between a container (e.g. linux/srl node) and an `ovs-bridge` node, the ovs endpoint is an `EndpointBridge` whose node is the ovs node, and the other endpoint is an `EndpointVeth` on the container node. Let me check how a veth link deploys when one endpoint is a bridge node — `LinkVEth.Deploy` handles the bridge endpoint by calling `node.AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link, SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep))` on the bridge node (the ovs node). Let me confirm by reading link_veth.go Deploy.

22: // ToLinkBriefRaw converts the raw link into a LinkBriefRaw.
23: func (r *LinkVEthRaw) ToLinkBriefRaw() *LinkBriefRaw {
24: 	lc := &LinkBriefRaw{
25: 		Endpoints:        []string{},

27: 	}
28: 
29: 	for _, e := range r.Endpoints {

42: func (r *LinkVEthRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams) (Link, error) {
43: 	// filtered true means the link is in the filter provided by a user
44: 	// aka it should be resolved/created/deployed
45: 	filtered := isInFilter(params, r.Endpoints)
46: 	if !filtered {
47: 		return nil, nil
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	if r.fromBrief && r.briefDefaultLinkType(params) == LinkTypeVethStitch {
51: 		return NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth(r).Resolve(params)

54: 	// create LinkVEth struct
55: 	l := NewLinkVEth()
56: 	l.LinkCommonParams = r.LinkCommonParams
57: 
58: 	// Normalize link vars to ensure JSON serialization compatibility
59: 	l.Vars = normalizeVars(l.Vars)
60: 
61: 	// resolve raw endpoints (epr) to endpoints (ep)
62: 	for _, epr := range r.Endpoints {
63: 		ep, err := epr.Resolve(params, l)
64: 		if err != nil {
65: 			return nil, err
66: 		}

68: 		// add endpoint to the link endpoints

70: 	}

75: 	}

166: func (l *LinkVEth) deployAEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
167: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
168: 	// the peer Endpoint is the other of the two endpoints in the
169: 	// Endpoints slice. So do a +1 on the index and modulo operation
170: 	// to take care of the wrap around.
171: 	peerIdx := (idx + 1) % 2
172: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[peerIdx]
173: 
174: 	log.Debugf("Creating Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
175: 
176: 	// build the netlink.Veth struct for the link provisioning
177: 	linkA := &netlink.Veth{
178: 		LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
179: 			Name: ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
180: 			MTU:  l.MTU,
181: 			// Mac address is set later on
182: 		},
183: 		PeerName: peerEp.GetRandIfaceName(),
184: 		// PeerMac address is set later on
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	// add the link
188: 	err := netlink.LinkAdd(linkA)
189: 	if err != nil {
190: 		return err
191: 	}
192: 
193: 	// cleanup is a helper that removes the veth pair if a subsequent step fails
194: 	// after LinkAdd succeeded, preventing orphaned interfaces from blocking retries.
195: 	cleanup := func(err error) error {
196: 		if delErr := netlink.LinkDel(linkA); delErr != nil {
197: 			log.Debugf(
198: 				"failed to cleanup veth pair %s after error: %v",
199: 				ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
200: 				delErr,
201: 			)
202: 		}
203: 		return err
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	// disable TXOffloading
207: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
208: 		return cleanup(err)
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	// the link needs to be moved to the relevant network namespace
212: 	// and enabled (up). This is done via linkSetupFunc.
213: 	// based on the endpoint type the link setup function is different.
214: 	// linkSetupFunc is executed in a netns of a node.
215: 	// if the node is a regular namespace node
216: 	// add link to node, rename, set mac and Up
217: 	err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, linkA,
218: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(linkA, ep))
219: 	if err != nil {
220: 		return cleanup(err)
221: 	}
222: 
223: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
224: 
225: 	// e.g. host endpoints are nodeless, and therefore the B end of the veth link should
226: 	// be deployed right after the A end is deployed.
227: 	if peerEp.IsNodeless() {
228: 		return l.deployBEnd(ctx, peerIdx)
229: 	}
230: 
231: 	return nil
232: }
233: 
234: func (l *LinkVEth) deployBEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
235: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
236: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[(idx+1)%2]
237: 
238: 	log.Debugf("Assigning Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
239: 
240: 	// retrieve the netlink.Link for the provided Endpoint
241: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ep.GetRandIfaceName())
242: 	if err != nil {
243: 		return err
244: 	}
245: 
246: 	// disable TXOffloading
247: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
248: 		return err
249: 	}
250: 
251: 	// Host endpoints already live in the current namespace; set them up in place.
252: 	// Other nodeless endpoints, such as the management bridge, still need their
253: 	// node-specific setup.
254: 	if ep.IsNodeless() && ep.GetNode().GetLinkEndpointType() == LinkEndpointTypeHost {
255: 		if err := SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep)(nil); err != nil {
256: 			return err
257: 		}
258: 	} else if err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link,
259: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep)); err != nil {
260: 		return err
261: 	}
262: 
263: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed
264: 
265: 	if len(l.Endpoints) == 2 {
266: 		log.Infof("Created link: %s ▪┄┄▪ %s", l.Endpoints[0], l.Endpoints[1])
267: 	}
268: 
269: 	return nil
270: }
271: 
272: // getEndpointIndex returns the index of the ep endpoint belonging to l link.
273: // An error is returned when the ep is not part of the l's endpoints.
274: func (l *LinkVEth) getEndpointIndex(ep Endpoint) (int, error) {
275: 	for idx, e := range l.Endpoints {
276: 		if e == ep {
277: 			return idx, nil
278: 		}
279: 	}
280: 
281: 	// if the endpoint is not part of the link
282: 	// build a string list of endpoints and return a meaningful error
283: 	var epStrings []string
284: 	for _, e := range l.Endpoints {
285: 		epStrings = append(epStrings, e.String())
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	return -1, fmt.Errorf(
289: 		"endpoint %s does not belong to link [ %s ]",
290: 		ep.String(),
291: 		strings.Join(epStrings, ", "),
292: 	)
293: }
294: 
295: // Deploy deploys the veth link by creating the A and B sides of the veth pair independently
296: // based on the calling endpoint.
297: func (l *LinkVEth) Deploy(ctx context.Context, ep Endpoint) error {
298: 	// since each node calls deploy on its links, we need to make sure that we only deploy
299: 	// the link once, even if multiple nodes call deploy on the same link.
300: 	l.deployMutex.Lock()
301: 	defer l.deployMutex.Unlock()
302: 
303: 	// first we need to check that the provided ep is part of this link
304: 	idx, err := l.getEndpointIndex(ep)
305: 	if err != nil {
306: 		return err
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	// Retry transient netlink errors that can occur during concurrent link operations.
310: 	// deployAEnd cleans up partial state on failure, making each retry idempotent.
311: 	return retryTransientNetlink(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("deploy link %s", ep), func() error {
312: 		switch l.DeploymentState {
313: 		case LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed:
314: 			return l.deployBEnd(ctx, idx)
315: 		case LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed:
316: 			return nil
317: 		default:
318: 			return l.deployAEnd(ctx, idx)
319: 		}
320: 	})
321: }
322: 
323: func (*LinkVEth) PostDeploy(context.Context) error {
324: 	return nil
325: }
326: 
327: func (l *LinkVEth) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
328: 	l.deployMutex.Lock()
329: 	defer l.deployMutex.Unlock()
330: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {
331: 		return nil
332: 	}
333: 	for _, ep := range l.GetEndpoints() {
334: 		err := ep.Remove(ctx)
335: 		if err != nil {
336: 			log.Debug(err)
337: 		}
338: 	}
339: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
340: 	return nil
341: }
342: 
343: func (l *LinkVEth) GetEndpoints() []Endpoint {
344: 	return l.Endpoints
345: }
346: 
347: func (l *LinkVEth) GetRuntimeEndpoints() []Endpoint {
348: 	return l.GetEndpoints()
349: }

1: ---
2: search:
3:   boost: 4
4: kind_code_name: ovs-bridge
5: kind_display_name: Openvswitch bridge
6: ---
7: # -{{ kind_display_name }}-
8: 
9: -{{ kind_display_name }}- is identified with `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md).
10: 
11: Similar to [linux bridge](bridge.md) capability, containerlab allows to connect nodes to an Openvswitch (Ovs) bridge. Ovs bridges offers even more connectivity options compared to classic Linux bridge, as well as it allows to create stretched L2 domain by means of tunneled interfaces (vxlan).
12: 
13: ## Using ovs-bridge kind
14: Containerlab doesn't create bridges on users behalf, that means that in order to use a bridge in the [topology definition file](../topo-def-file.md), the Ovs bridge needs to be created first.
15: 
16: Once the bridge is created, it has to be referenced as a node inside the topology file:
17: 
18: ```yaml
19: name: ovs
20: 
21: topology:
22:   nodes:
23:     myovs:
24:       kind: -{{ kind_code_name }}-
25:     ceos:
26:       kind: arista_ceos
27:       image: ceos:latest
28:   links:
29:     - endpoints: ["myovs:ovsp1", "srl:eth1"]
30: 
31: ```
32: 
33: In the example above, node `myovs` of kind `-{{ kind_code_name }}-` tells containerlab to identify it as a Ovs bridge and look for a bridge named `myovs`.
34: 
35: When connecting other nodes to a bridge, the bridge endpoint must be present in the `links` section.
36: 
37: !!!note
38:     When choosing names of the interfaces that need to be connected to the bridge make sure that these names are not clashing with existing interfaces.  
39:     In the example above we attach a single interfaces named `ovsp1` to the Ovs bridge with a name `myovs`. Before that, we ensured that no other interfaces named `ovsp1` existed.
40: 
41: As a result of such topology definition, you will see the Ovs bridge `br-clab` with three interfaces attached to it:
42: 
43: ```
44: ❯ ovs-vsctl show
45: 918a3466-4368-4167-9162-f2cf80a0c106
46:     Bridge myovs
47:         Port myovs
48:             Interface myovs
49:                 type: internal
50:         Port eth1
51:             Interface ovsp1
52:     ovs_version: "2.13.1"
53: ```

(End of file - total 53 lines)

630: 		workers = uint(len(nodes))

Reasoning
Good: for the OVS node, `ExecFunction` runs in the current (root) namespace, so `ovs-vsctl` calls via `exec.Command` and `netlink` calls operate on the host — correct.

Important: `RemoveOwnedInterface` is called with `ref.node` — the node for the endpoint. For an OVS endpoint, node = ovs node → ExecFunction = root ns → netlink LinkByName(sanitized) in root ns → correct (the OVS port netdev lives in the root ns). Good.

But wait — for a regular container node endpoint, `ExecFunction` requires the container netns to be joinable. During destroy, if the container is already gone, `ExecFunction` returns an error "cannot exec a command..."? In destroy flow, links are removed BEFORE containers are deleted? Let me check the destroy ordering: does destroy remove links first or delete containers first? If links are removed after container deletion, ExecFunction fails... but that's pre-existing behavior of RemoveOwnedInterface (also present before the PR). The PR changed Remove to call removeBridgePort — inside ExecFunction, so if ExecFunction fails, the OVS port cleanup never runs. Hmm — during `destroy`, is `LinkVEth.Remove` (→ EndpointGeneric.Remove → ExecFunction) called? Let me check destroy.go for link removal.

Reasoning
This is about veth-stitch, not directly about OVS port removal with filters. The filtered cleanup only handles stitch alt names. For plain veth links with an OVS endpoint, when a node filter excludes the OVS node, `CleanupFilteredLinks` only calls `cleanupFilteredLink` for veth and veth-stitched raws; for plain veth (`LinkVEthRaw.cleanupFilteredLink`), it calls `cleanupFilteredVethStitch` — which only handles stitched alt names (for plain veth, StitchAltName names won't exist; no-op). So when a plain veth link has an OVS endpoint and the filter excludes the OVS node, who removes the OVS side?

Let me look at how destroy handles link removal when nodes are filtered — there must be other machinery (`c.nodeFilter`, deleteNodes removes links of included nodes?). Let me check `deleteNodes` and where links are removed during filtered destroy.

Reasoning
The destroy flow: `CleanupFilteredLinks` (only cleans stitch interfaces for filtered nodes), then `deleteNodes` which deletes each node (including the OVS node if not filtered out) — the OVS `Delete` now sweeps stale auto ports. But wait — in destroy, are regular veth links removed before `deleteNodes`? Where does `LinkVEth.Remove` get called during destroy? `CleanupFilteredLinks` is only for the filtered case. For non-filtered destroy, links are removed... by deleting containers (veth endpoints vanish) and the OVS port? The OVS port named `clab-*` — for an OVS bridge node, `n.Delete(ctx)` → `ovs.Delete` — the new sweep removes stale `clab-*` ports. That's precisely why the sweep was added in `Delete`. And named ports (valid names) — `ovs.Delete`... does it call removeEndpointPorts for each endpoint? It iterates `n.GetEndpoints()`; endpoints are populated only if topology known. In destroy-by-topology, the OVS node's endpoints are registered. OK.

So the sweep in `Delete` is the safety net. Good design, consistent with the PR description.

147: func (n *ovs) AddLinkToContainer(
148: 	ctx context.Context,
149: 	link netlink.Link,
150: 	f func(ns.NetNS) error,
151: ) error {
152: 	// retrieve the namespace handle
153: 	curNamespace, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
154: 	if err != nil {
155: 		return err
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	// execute the given function
159: 	err = curNamespace.Do(f)
160: 	if err != nil {
161: 		return err
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	// need to reread the link, due to the changed the function f might have applied to
165: 	// the link. Usually it renames the link to its final name.
166: 	link, err = netlink.LinkByIndex(link.Attrs().Index)
167: 	if err != nil {
168: 		return err
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	name := link.Attrs().Name
172: 	logical := n.logicalEndpointName(link)
173: 	args := []string{"--may-exist", "add-port", n.Cfg.ShortName, name}
174: 	// A port named after the interface is reused by --may-exist and keeps its config. A random
175: 	// netdev name needs a tag, so that a later attach or link removal can find the port. The full
176: 	// stale-port sweep runs once from Delete, not on every attach.
177: 	if logical != name {
178: 		if err := n.removeEndpointPorts(logical); err != nil {
179: 			return err
180: 		}
181: 		args = append(args,
182: 			"--", "set", "Interface", name,
183: 			"external_ids:"+ovsEndpointExtID+"="+ovsMapValue(logical),
184: 		)
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	out, err := ovsVsctl(args...)
188: 	if err != nil {
189: 		return fmt.Errorf("add OVS port %q as %q: %w (%s)", name, logical, err, out)
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	return nil
193: }

252: 	}

258: // side of the veth removes the device and leaves the OVS port in place under that random name.
259: func (n *ovs) removeMissingAutoPorts() error {
260: 	if n.Cfg == nil || n.Cfg.ShortName == "" {
261: 		return nil
262: 	}

314: func ovsInterfaceNames(condition string) ([]string, error) {
315: 	out, err := ovsVsctl(
316: 		"--format=csv",
317: 		"--no-headings",
318: 		"--data=bare",
319: 		"--columns=name",
320: 		"find",
321: 		"Interface",

323: 	)

330: 		return nil, nil
331: 	}

334: }

336: func ovsInterfaceDeviceMissing(iface string) (bool, error) {
337: 	out, err := ovsVsctl("--data=bare", "get", "Interface", iface, "error")
338: 	if err != nil {
339: 		// The port disappeared between ListPorts and this get. Nothing left to delete.
340: 		if ovsRowMissing(string(out)) {
341: 			return false, nil
342: 		}
343: 		return false, fmt.Errorf("get OVS interface %q error: %w (%s)", iface, err, out)
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	return ovsDeviceMissing(string(out)), nil
347: }

349: // ovsDeviceMissing reports whether an OVS interface error column says the netdev is gone.
350: // A live interface returns "[]".
351: func ovsDeviceMissing(errorColumn string) bool {
352: 	errorColumn = strings.TrimSpace(errorColumn)
353: 
354: 	return strings.Contains(errorColumn, "could not open network device")
355: }

357: func ovsRowMissing(output string) bool {
358: 	return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(output), "no row")
359: }

361: func ovsMapValue(value string) string {
362: 	if value == "" {
363: 		return `""`
364: 	}
365: 	for _, r := range value {
366: 		switch {
367: 		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
368: 		case strings.ContainsRune("-_.:@", r):
369: 		default:
370: 			return fmt.Sprintf("%q", value)
371: 		}
372: 	}

When that name is not a valid\n200: // Linux interface name, the netdev keeps a random clab-* name and the topology name is an altname.\n201: func (n *ovs) logicalEndpointName(link netlink.Link) string {\n202: \tif link == nil {\n203: \t\treturn \"\"\n204: \t}\n205: \n206: \tname := link.Attrs().Name\n207: \talts := make(map[string]struct{}, len(link.Attrs().AltNames))\n208: \tfor _, alt := range link.Attrs().AltNames {\n209: \t\talts[alt] = struct{}{}\n210: \t}\n211: \n212: \tfor _, ep := range n.GetEndpoints() {\n213: \t\tiface := ep.GetIfaceName()\n214: \t\tif iface == name {\n215: \t\t\treturn iface\n216: \t\t}\n217: \t\tif _, ok := alts[clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(iface)]; ok {\n218: \t\t\treturn iface\n219: \t\t}\n220: \t}\n221: \n222: \treturn name\n223: }\n224: \n225: // removeEndpointPorts deletes the ports on this bridge tagged with the topology interface name.\n226: func (n *ovs) removeEndpointPorts(endpoint string) error {\n227: \tif endpoint == \"\" || n.Cfg == nil || n.Cfg.ShortName == \"\" {\n228: \t\treturn nil\n229: \t}\n230: \n231: \tc := goOvs.New(goOvs.Timeout(ovsTimeoutSeconds))\n232: \n233: \tnames, err := ovsInterfaceNames(\n234: \t\t\"external_ids:\" + ovsEndpointExtID + \"=\" + ovsMapValue(endpoint),\n235: \t)\n236: \tif err != nil {\n237: \t\treturn err\n238: \t}\n239: \n240: \tonBridge, err := bridgePortSet(c, n.Cfg.ShortName)\n241: \tif err != nil {\n242: \t\treturn err\n243: \t}\n244: \n245: \tfor _, name := range names {\n246: \t\tif _, ok := onBridge[name]; !ok {\n247: \t\t\tcontinue\n248: \t\t}\n249: \t\tif err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, name); err != nil {\n250: \t\t\treturn err\n251: \t\t}\n252: \t}\n253: \n254: \treturn nil\n255: }\n256: \n257: // removeMissingAutoPorts deletes clab-* ports whose netdev is already gone. Deleting the container\n258: // side of the veth removes the device and leaves the OVS port in place under that random name.\n259: func (n *ovs) removeMissingAutoPorts() error {\n260: \tif n.Cfg == nil || n.Cfg.ShortName == \"\" {\n261: \t\treturn nil\n262: \t}\n263: \n264: \tc := goOvs.New(goOvs.Timeout(ovsTimeoutSeconds))\n265: \tports, err := c.VSwitch.ListPorts(n.Cfg.ShortName)\n266: \tif err != nil {\n267: \t\treturn err\n268: \t}\n269: \n270: \tfor _, port := range ports {\n271: \t\tif !clabAutoPort.MatchString(port) {\n272: \t\t\tcontinue\n273: \t\t}\n274: \t\tmissing, err := ovsInterfaceDeviceMissing(port)\n275: \t\tif err != nil {\n276: \t\t\treturn err\n277: \t\t}\n278: \t\tif !missing {\n279: \t\t\tcontinue\n280: \t\t}\n281: \t\tlog.Debugf(\n282: \t\t\t\"Removing stale OVS port %q from bridge %q\",\n283: \t\t\tport,\n284: \t\t\tn.Cfg.ShortName,\n285: \t\t)\n286: \t\tif err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(n.Cfg.ShortName, port); err != nil {\n287: \t\t\treturn err\n288: \t\t}\n289: \t}\n290: \n291: \treturn nil\n292: }\n293: \n294: func bridgePortSet(c *goOvs.Client, bridge string) (map[string]struct{}, error) {\n295: \tports, err := c.VSwitch.ListPorts(bridge)\n296: \tif err != nil {\n297: \t\treturn nil, err\n298: \t}\n299: \n300: \tset := make(map[string]struct{}, len(ports))\n301: \tfor _, port := range ports {\n302: \t\tset[port] = struct{}{}\n303: \t}\n304: \n305: \treturn set, nil\n306: }\n307: \n308: func ovsVsctl(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {\n309: \targs = append([]string{fmt.Sprintf(\"--timeout=%d\", ovsTimeoutSeconds)}, args...)\n310: \n311: \treturn exec.Command(\"ovs-vsctl\", args...).CombinedOutput()\n312: }\n313: \n314: func ovsInterfaceNames(condition string) ([]string, error) {\n315: \tout, err := ovsVsctl(\n316: \t\t\"--format=csv\",\n317: \t\t\"--no-headings\",\n318: \t\t\"--data=bare\",\n319: \t\t\"--columns=name\",\n320: \t\t\"find\",\n321: \t\t\"Interface\",\n322: \t\tcondition,\n323: \t)\n324: \tif err != nil {\n325: \t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"find OVS interfaces: %w (%s)\", err, out)\n326: \t}\n327: \n328: \ttext := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))\n329: \tif text == \"\" {\n330: \t\treturn nil, nil\n331: \t}\n332: \n333: \treturn strings.Split(text, \"\\n\"), nil\n334: }\n335: \n336: func ovsInterfaceDeviceMissing(iface string) (bool, error) {\n337: \tout, err := ovsVsctl(\"--data=bare\", \"get\", \"Interface\", iface, \"error\")\n338: \tif err != nil {\n339: \t\t// The port disappeared between ListPorts and this get. Nothing left to delete.\n340: \t\tif ovsRowMissing(string(out)) {\n341: \t\t\treturn false, nil\n342: \t\t}\n343: \t\treturn false, fmt.Errorf(\"get OVS interface %q error: %w (%s)\", iface, err, out)\n344: \t}\n345: \n346: \treturn ovsDeviceMissing(string(out)), nil\n347: }\n348: \n349: // ovsDeviceMissing reports whether an OVS interface error column says the netdev is gone.\n350: // A live interface returns \"[]\".\n351: func ovsDeviceMissing(errorColumn string) bool {\n352: \terrorColumn = strings.TrimSpace(errorColumn)\n353: \n354: \treturn strings.Contains(errorColumn, \"could not open network device\")\n355: }\n356: \n357: func ovsRowMissing(output string) bool {\n358: \treturn strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(output), \"no row\")\n359: }\n360: \n361: func ovsMapValue(value string) string {\n362: \tif value == \"\" {\n363: \t\treturn `\"\"`\n364: \t}\n365: \tfor _, r := range value {\n366: \t\tswitch {\n367: \t\tcase r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':\n368: \t\tcase strings.ContainsRune(\"-_.:@\", r):\n369: \t\tdefault:\n370: \t\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%q\", value)\n371: \t\t}\n372: \t}\n373: \n374: \treturn value\n375: }\n\n(End of file - total 375 lines)\n</content>",

Reasoning
Both call sites pass the endpoint's own node (`ep.GetNode()`, `ref.node`). For OVS endpoints, `ref.node` is the OVS node → `ExecFunction` runs in root ns → `netlink.LinkByName(sanitized)` + `removeBridgePort` → tagged-port removal. Good — apply/reconcile deletions of OVS endpoints now clean tagged ports.

One important check: `RemoveOwnedInterface` calls `removeBridgePort` ONLY when `netlink.LinkByName(sanitized)` SUCCEEDS (link found). If the netdev is already gone (e.g., container deleted, OVS-side netdev destroyed), `LinkByName` fails with notfound → in the notfound branch, `removeBridgePort(ref.node, ifaceName)` is called — with the SANITIZED name as `ifaceName`? Since `removeEndpointPorts` matches by tag (logical name), passing the raw `ifaceName` is what we want (the tag value is the topology name). Let me re-read the relevant lines.

198: // interface name Linux will not accept are named after the random netdev, so deleting the veth
199: // from the container side leaves the port behind.
200: type bridgePortDeleter interface {
201: 	DeleteBridgePort(string) error
202: }
203: 
204: func removeBridgePort(node Node, ifaceName string) error {
205: 	if node == nil || ifaceName == "" {
206: 		return nil
207: 	}
208: 
209: 	cleaner, ok := node.(bridgePortDeleter)
210: 	if !ok {
211: 		return nil
212: 	}
213: 
214: 	// Best-effort, matching ovs.Delete. A missing bridge or a down ovsdb must not abort
215: 	// destroy or reconcile and leave the container running.
216: 	if err := cleaner.DeleteBridgePort(ifaceName); err != nil {
217: 		log.Errorf(
218: 			"Could not remove bridge port %q on node %q: %v",
219: 			ifaceName,
220: 			node.GetShortName(),
221: 			err,
222: 		)
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	return nil
226: }
227: 
228: // isOwnedBy reports whether link carries the ownership marker of the logical
229: // endpoint ownerName:ifaceName. Interfaces of mgmt-net links deployed by earlier
230: // releases carry a marker for the bridge name of the mgmt-net link node instead
231: // of the stable mgmt-net owner name, and are accepted as well.
232: func isOwnedBy(link netlink.Link, node Node, ownerName, ifaceName string) bool {
233: 	if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, ownerName, ifaceName) {
234: 		return true
235: 	}
236: 
237: 	if _, ok := node.(*mgmtBridgeLinkNode); ok && ownerName == mgmtNetOwnerName {
238: 		return HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, node.GetShortName(), ifaceName)
239: 	}
240: 
241: 	return false
242: }

99: 	}

101: 		t.Fatalf("peer delete left %v, want the stale port", ports)
102: 	}
103: 
104: 	// An untagged port may belong to the operator and is not removed for a topology interface.

106: 		t.Fatalf("add operator port: %v (%s)", err, out)
107: 	}
108: 	if err := n.DeleteBridgePort("operator-port"); err != nil {
109: 		t.Fatalf("delete bridge port: %v", err)
110: 	}
111: 	if ports := dataPorts(t, bridge); len(ports) != 2 {
112: 		t.Fatalf("ports after untagged delete = %v, want the operator port kept", ports)
113: 	}
114: 	if err := c.VSwitch.DeletePort(bridge, "operator-port"); err != nil {
115: 		t.Fatalf("delete operator port: %v", err)
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	// A port named after the interface keeps its config across a reattach.
119: 	isNamedPort := dataPorts(t, bridge)[0] == endpoint
120: 	if isNamedPort {
121: 		if out, err := ovsVsctl("set", "Port", endpoint, "tag=100"); err != nil {
122: 			t.Fatalf("set tag: %v (%s)", err, out)
123: 		}
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	second, secondPeer := addVethPair(t)

128: 	if err := n.AddLinkToContainer(
129: 		context.Background(),
130: 		second,
131: 		clablinks.SetNameMACAndUpInterface(second, ep),
132: 	); err != nil {
133: 		t.Fatalf("reattach: %v", err)
134: 	}

136: 		t.Fatalf("ports after reattach = %v, want 1", ports)
137: 	}

140: 		if err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(string(out)) != "100" {
141: 			t.Fatalf("tag after reattach = %q, err = %v, want 100", out, err)
142: 		}
143: 	}
144:

146: 		t.Fatalf("delete node: %v", err)
147: 	}

150: 	}

Reasoning
`applyKnownEndpointNames` returns nil unless nodeName is `host` or `mgmt-net`. For an OVS node, `DiscoverOwnedInterfacesFor` is called with `knownIfaceNames = nil` → no name filtering → the OVS-side `clab-xxxx` netdev (which carries the ownership altname) IS discovered. ✓ Reconcile sees it, matching the desired endpoint via `endpointKeyFromEndpoint` — but wait: the live endpoint key uses `iface.Name` = `clab-xxxx`, while the desired endpoint key uses the topology iface name `ixr-dut-30-e1-10`. So matching desired ↔ live might fail → reconcile treats it as missing/extra → remove + re-add. Let me look at how desired endpoints are matched against live endpoints — `endpointKeyFromEndpoint` uses `GetIfaceName` presumably. If mismatch, `deleteApplyEndpoints` + redeploy each apply — meaning every `apply` tears down and re-adds OVS endpoints with invalid names? Hmm — that's pre-existing behavior for invalid names though (netdev was always random pre-PR). Let me check whether matching handles altname mapping. Search for `endpointKeyFromEndpoint` and how liveEndpointSet is matched with desired.

<content>
1: # Release 0.82
2: 
3: :material-calendar: 2026-10-22 · :material-list-status: [Full Changelog](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/releases)
4: 
5: ## New `mikrotik_chr` kind
6: 
7: Containerlab can now run MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the [official `mikrotik/chr` image](https://hub.docker.com/r/mikrotik/chr) with the [new `mikrotik_chr` kind](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md). The image is used as is - no [vrnetlab](../manual/vrnetlab.md) build - and is published for `amd64` and `arm64`, booting with KVM when `/dev/kvm` is available and falling back to QEMU's TCG emulation otherwise:
8: 
9: ```yaml
10: topology:
11:   nodes:
12:     r1:
13:       kind: mikrotik_chr
14:       image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5
15:       startup-config: r1.rsc
16:   links:
17:     - endpoints: ["r1:ether2", "r2:ether2"]
18: ```
19: 
20: Management is transparent by default: the node's management address is RouterOS's own `ether1` address, so SSH, REST, Winbox, the RouterOS API, SNMP and LLDP all reply directly on the address containerlab assigned, and the IPv4/IPv6 shown in the `inspect` table are the ones configured in RouterOS. Data interfaces map in order - container `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)` - with the MTU copied from the veth.
21: 
22: To make the original image work with the reach Containerlab's featureset, an embedded launcher script has been added to the original image. This script handles bootstrap over the image's REST API (credentials, identity and `startup-config`), readiness detection backed by a default healthcheck so [`wait-for: healthy`](../manual/nodes.md#wait-for) and `stages` ordering work, and restarts - `containerlab restart`, a Docker restart or an in-router reboot - that keep interface names, MACs, configuration and links intact. Custom [`credentials`](../manual/nodes.md#credentials) create the user in the `full` group and disable the factory `admin` account, which has a blank password on a fresh CHR disk.
23: 
24: The original [`mikrotik_ros`](../manual/kinds/vr-ros.md) kind - CHR from an image built with vrnetlab - is untouched, and both kinds share the interface naming and startup-config conventions, so a lab moves between them by changing `kind` and `image`.
25: 
26: See the [`mikrotik_chr` kind documentation](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md).
27: 
28: Done in #3498 thanks to @lz-networks
29: 
30: ## SR-SIM
31: 
32: ### Custom startup credentials
33: 
34: The SR OS startup configuration that containerlab generates for SR-SIM nodes renders the admin user and password from the node [`credentials`](../manual/nodes.md#credentials) key instead of hardcoding `admin` / `NokiaSros1!`. For model-driven nodes the generated configuration grants console, gRPC and NETCONF access to that user, and the postdeploy SSH and NETCONF operations use the same credentials. When `credentials` are not set, the defaults stay unchanged.
35: 
36: ### Version-aware startup templates
37: 
38: The model-driven startup template is split by SR OS release. Releases up to 26.3 keep the CCM8 TLS cipher their TLS bootstrap relies on, while SR OS 26.7, later releases and development images - which report version `0.0.0` - use a template without it. The obsolete `system grpc md-cli` and `md-cli-session` lines are emitted only for releases up to 25.10. The classic SR, IXR and SAR templates follow the same CCM8 cutoff.
39: 
40: ### Integrated chassis tweaks
41: 
42: * `components` entries with a `type` set the `NOKIA_SROS_CARD` variable and skip the generated card and MDA configuration.
43: * Node-level `env` overrides `components`: when the same variable is set to different values, the environment variable wins and containerlab logs a warning naming it.
44: * `ixr-r6` accepts `components` in both slots `A` and `B`, with one container per CPM, making a proper dual-CPIOM node.
45: * User component overrides no longer fail the deployment.
46: * At deploy time containerlab reads `chassis_info.json` from the selected SR-SIM image and compares the effective `components` configuration with the hardware types listed for the chassis. Unsupported slots and card, SFM, XIOM or MDA types produce warnings without stopping the deployment.
47: 
48: Done in #3446, #3488 thanks @sacckth and @kaelemc
49: 
50: ## Arch Linux support
51: 
52: The installation script now detects Arch-based systems and its package manager, and installs the `containerlab-bin` package from the aur package repository. Note, that currently only linux/amd64 variant is available, so on linux/arm64 systems download the package from our github releases.
53: 
54: 
55: ## Miscellaneous
56: 
57: - `inspect` no longer errors on a partially built lab: containers that were not created are skipped, so a lab whose deployment failed midway can still be inspected. [#3516](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3516)
58: - `destroy --cleanup` no longer removes unrelated `clab-*` directories when a lab has no running containers: the lab directory is resolved deterministically from the topology name, mismatched directories are refused with a warning, and a missing directory is a no-op. [#3501](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3501)
59: - TX checksum offload management is reapplied on every start for the `cisco_iol` and `linux` kinds. A stop/start cycle recreates the management veth and resets the offload settings to their defaults, which broke TCP/UDP connectivity of IOL nodes. [#3510](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3510)
60: - Parked link endpoints survive a failed restore: the parking network namespace is kept on the node - and reused by a subsequent park/restore cycle - so the parked endpoints can be recovered instead of being lost. [#3506](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3506)
61: - The `c9s` runtime stamps every c9s Node object and the stored topology definition with a `c9s.run/originalNodeName` label holding the node name exactly as the clab file spells it, so tooling that only sees the clab file can select the c9s nodes by their original names even though the cluster objects carry sanitized names. The label key is reserved: a value set for it in the topology file is overwritten on every deploy. [#3509](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3509)
62:

This script handles bootstrap over the image's REST API (credentials, identity and `startup-config`), readiness detection backed by a default healthcheck so [`wait-for: healthy`](../manual/nodes.md#wait-for) and `stages` ordering work, and restarts - `containerlab restart`, a Docker restart or an in-router reboot - that keep interface names, MACs, configuration and links intact. Unsupported slots and card, SFM, XIOM or MDA types produce warnings without stopping the deployment.\n47: \n48: Done in #3446, #3488 thanks @sacckth and @kaelemc\n49: \n50: ## Arch Linux support\n51: \n52: The installation script now detects Arch-based systems and its package manager, and installs the `containerlab-bin` package from the aur package repository.         "text": "# Release 0.82\n\n:material-calendar: 2026-10-22 · :material-list-status: [Full Changelog](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/releases)\n\n## New `mikrotik_chr` kind\n\nContainerlab can now run MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the [official `mikrotik/chr` image](https://hub.docker.com/r/mikrotik/chr) with the [new `mikrotik_chr` kind](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md). The image is used as is - no [vrnetlab](../manual/vrnetlab.md) build - and is published for `amd64` and `arm64`, booting with KVM when `/dev/kvm` is available and falling back to QEMU's TCG emulation otherwise:\n\n```yaml\ntopology:\n  nodes:\n    r1:\n      kind: mikrotik_chr\n      image: mikrotik/chr:7.24.5\n      startup-config: r1.rsc\n  links:\n    - endpoints: [\"r1:ether2\", \"r2:ether2\"]\n```\n\nManagement is transparent by default: the node's management address is RouterOS's own `ether1` address, so SSH, REST, Winbox, the RouterOS API, SNMP and LLDP all reply directly on the address containerlab assigned, and the IPv4/IPv6 shown in the `inspect` table are the ones configured in RouterOS. Data interfaces map in order - container `ethN` is RouterOS `ether(N+1)` - with the MTU copied from the veth.\n\nTo make the original image work with the reach Containerlab's featureset, an embedded launcher script has been added to the original image. This script handles bootstrap over the image's REST API (credentials, identity and `startup-config`), readiness detection backed by a default healthcheck so [`wait-for: healthy`](../manual/nodes.md#wait-for) and `stages` ordering work, and restarts - `containerlab restart`, a Docker restart or an in-router reboot - that keep interface names, MACs, configuration and links intact. Custom [`credentials`](../manual/nodes.md#credentials) create the user in the `full` group and disable the factory `admin` account, which has a blank password on a fresh CHR disk.\n\nThe original [`mikrotik_ros`](../manual/kinds/vr-ros.md) kind - CHR from an image built with vrnetlab - is untouched, and both kinds share the interface naming and startup-config conventions, so a lab moves between them by changing `kind` and `image`.\n\nSee the [`mikrotik_chr` kind documentation](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md).\n\nDone in #3498 thanks to @lz-networks\n\n## SR-SIM\n\n### Custom startup credentials\n\nThe SR OS startup configuration that containerlab generates for SR-SIM nodes renders the admin user and password from the node [`credentials`](../manual/nodes.md#credentials) key instead of hardcoding `admin` / `NokiaSros1!`. For model-driven nodes the generated configuration grants console, gRPC and NETCONF access to that user, and the postdeploy SSH and NETCONF operations use the same credentials. When `credentials` are not set, the defaults stay unchanged.\n\n### Version-aware startup templates\n\nThe model-driven startup template is split by SR OS release. Releases up to 26.3 keep the CCM8 TLS cipher their TLS bootstrap relies on, while SR OS 26.7, later releases and development images - which report version `0.0.0` - use a template without it. The obsolete `system grpc md-cli` and `md-cli-session` lines are emitted only for releases up to 25.10. The classic SR, IXR and SAR templates follow the same CCM8 cutoff.\n\n### Integrated chassis tweaks\n\n* `components` entries with a `type` set the `NOKIA_SROS_CARD` variable and skip the generated card and MDA configuration.\n* Node-level `env` overrides `components`: when the same variable is set to different values, the environment variable wins and containerlab logs a warning naming it.\n* `ixr-r6` accepts `components` in both slots `A` and `B`, with one container per CPM, making a proper dual-CPIOM node.\n* User component overrides no longer fail the deployment.\n* At deploy time containerlab reads `chassis_info.json` from the selected SR-SIM image and compares the effective `components` configuration with the hardware types listed for the chassis. Unsupported slots and card, SFM, XIOM or MDA types produce warnings without stopping the deployment.\n\nDone in #3446, #3488 thanks @sacckth and @kaelemc\n\n## Arch Linux support\n\nThe installation script now detects Arch-based systems and its package manager, and installs the `containerlab-bin` package from the aur package repository. Note, that currently only linux/amd64 variant is available, so on linux/arm64 systems download the package from our github releases.\n\n\n## Miscellaneous\n\n- `inspect` no longer errors on a partially built lab: containers that were not created are skipped, so a lab whose deployment failed midway can still be inspected. [#3516](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3516)\n- `destroy --cleanup` no longer removes unrelated `clab-*` directories when a lab has no running containers: the lab directory is resolved deterministically from the topology name, mismatched directories are refused with a warning, and a missing directory is a no-op. [#3501](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3501)\n- TX checksum offload management is reapplied on every start for the `cisco_iol` and `linux` kinds. A stop/start cycle recreates the management veth and resets the offload settings to their defaults, which broke TCP/UDP connectivity of IOL nodes. [#3510](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3510)\n- Parked link endpoints survive a failed restore: the parking network namespace is kept on the node - and reused by a subsequent park/restore cycle - so the parked endpoints can be recovered instead of being lost. [#3506](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3506)\n- The `c9s` runtime stamps every c9s Node object and the stored topology definition with a `c9s.run/originalNodeName` label holding the node name exactly as the clab file spells it, so tooling that only sees the clab file can select the c9s nodes by their original names even though the cluster objects carry sanitized names. The label key is reserved: a value set for it in the topology file is overwritten on every deploy. [#3509](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3509)\n",
